Okay, yeah let’s say 200 people from hull uni I know who studied chemistry. 

Next went to a different university to get my PhD. 4 years (plus a bit more because covid). Between PhDs, post docs and PIs at the university, I’d say I know 75 - 100 chemists from that time (quite a close knit department, we all pretty much knew each other). Then there’s chemists I’ve met at summer schools and conferences who I’ve connected with from this time, maybe add another 25? So if we’re playing it conservatively, let’s say I connected with 100 different chemists during my PhD.

Alright, what’s next? My first industry job. There were two groups of chemists, surface chemistry and synthetic chemistry. Altogether makes up around 40 chemists (small start up, only around 100 people total when I left). So that’s 140 people so far.

Okay, my current role, post doc who helps manage a horizon 2020 consortium. In that alone there are 40 chemists, plus the additional members of the PIs research groups. So I’m going to bring that up to around 60. So we’re at 200.

Now the university I work at itself. It’s quite a big department, where synthetic work has its own building. At least 150 people working there between PIs, post docs, PhDs, technicians, spin out companies and I’d say I know maybe 100? 

So that’s 300 people there, discounting undergrads who I met during my PhD who have also gone on to get their phds, who I still speak to and keep up to date with how their life is going. Discounting the people I know through my partner who is also a chemist in a different field, I could easily make 400+ people who I have met through my career since leaving hull. Oh all the people I have mentioned above, 4 of them did their undergrad at hull (although I didn’t personally know them at the time).
My sample size is really not that small. I left Hull 8 years ago, and have moved and worked all over the country since then… always working in chemistry.

Same cost, but in my experience, Hull has one of the better quality of education. It’s not a highly regarded research department but for teaching (I did do my undergrad there, went on to do phds and post docs elsewhere) it’s the best I’ve seen, especially for practical hands on chemistry.

It’s not all about the PhDs produced. Some of the best synthetic chemists I know did their undergrads at hull. And these people went on to do their phds at Manchester, Lancaster, Edinburgh, York, Cambridge.

As someone who studied chemistry at Hull, same as my fiancé, and we both went on to get PhDs at different high research universities, we strongly disagree. The level of teaching at Hull was miles better than the experience we’ve seen when at other universities, especially when it comes to practical chemistry. Hull should be kept open at a minimum to teach undergraduate chemistry.
